# Coding agent setup & developer resources

AI coding agents rely on training data that cuts off at a set date. Because of this, agents often suggest deprecated models (`gemini-1.5`), older SDKs (`google-generativeai`), or outdated code patterns.

Connecting your agent to official Gemini developer resources helps it write accurate code using current models, the `google-genai` SDK, and the [Interactions API](/docs/interactions-overview).

You can connect your coding agent to Gemini documentation, rules, and CLI tools in five ways:
## Summary of agent resources  {% id="summary" %}

| Resource | What it provides | Availability |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **[Gemini Agent Skills](/docs/coding-agents#available-skills)** | Step-by-step rules, SDK patterns, and helper scripts for specific features (`gemini-api-dev`, `gemini-live-api-dev`, `gemini-omni-flash-api`). | Pre-installed in [AI Studio Build](https://ai.studio/build); install with `skills.sh`, Context7, or Managed Agents. |
| **[Gemini Docs MCP Server](/docs/coding-agents#mcp-setup)** | Live search (`gemini_search_docs`) and full page reads (`gemini_get_doc`) across all documentation. | Supported in Claude Code, Cursor, OpenAI Codex, and VS Code. |
| **[Gemini API Plugin](/docs/coding-agents#gemini-api-plugin)** | Bundled package with official Gemini skills, the Docs MCP server, and API key tools. | Antigravity. |

| **[Machine-Readable Docs](/docs/coding-agents#machine-readable-docs)** | Clean Markdown pages, `llms.txt` indexes, and content negotiation headers. | All documentation pages on `aistudio.google.com/docs`. |
| **[Gemini API CLI](/docs/cli)** | Stateless CLI (`gemini-api`) to generate media, analyze files, and run managed agents from the shell without writing SDK code. | Install on macOS, Linux, or Windows with the install script, Go, or prebuilt binaries. |

# Install a specific skill globally with skills.sh
npx skills add google-gemini/gemini-skills --skill <skill-name> --global

# Or install with Context7
npx ctx7 skills install /google-gemini/gemini-skills <skill-name>
```

### Available skills  {% id="skills-catalog" %}

#### `gemini-api-dev` {% id="gemini-api-dev" %}

Skill for building applications with the [Interactions API](/docs/interactions-overview) and the official Gemini API SDKs (`google-genai` for Python and `@google/genai` for TypeScript). This skill covers:

- Text generation, multi-turn chat, streaming, structured outputs, and function calling
- Image generation, text-to-speech (TTS), and multimodal inputs
- Server-side conversation state management, background execution, Deep Research, and managed agents
- Current model names and migrating legacy `generateContent` or `google-generativeai` code

```bash
npx skills add google-gemini/gemini-skills --skill gemini-api-dev --global
```

#### `gemini-live-api-dev` {% id="gemini-live-api-dev" %}

Skill for building real-time audio and video streaming applications with the [Gemini Live API](/docs/live-api). This skill covers:

- WebSocket session management, ephemeral client tokens, and session resumption
- Streaming audio, video, and text with voice activity detection (VAD) and barge-in support
- Background reasoning (extended thinking), non-blocking asynchronous tool calls, transcription, and live speech translation

```bash
npx skills add google-gemini/gemini-skills --skill gemini-live-api-dev --global
```

#### `gemini-omni-flash-api` {% id="gemini-omni-flash-api" %}

Skill for generating and editing video with Gemini Omni Flash using the Interactions API. Includes helper scripts (`upload_file.py`, `generate_video.py`, `prep_video.py`, `inspect_video.py`) and covers:

- Text-to-video generation and prompt crafting
- First-and-last-frame transitions and reference-guided video generation
- Video extensions and media preprocessing workflows

```bash
npx skills add google-gemini/gemini-skills --skill gemini-omni-flash-api --global
```

### Mount skills in Managed Agents  {% id="managed-agents-skills" %}

When you run remote managed agents with the Interactions API, you can mount the `google-gemini/gemini-skills` repository into the agent's workspace. See the [Gemini API Skills guide](https://aistudio.google.com/learn/gemini-api-skills) for details:

```python
from google import genai

client = genai.Client(http_options={"api_version": "v1beta"})

## Connect the Gemini Docs MCP server  {% id="mcp-setup" %}

The public **Gemini Docs MCP server** (`https://gemini-api-docs-mcp.dev`) gives your agent live access to the entire documentation site. Your agent can search and read documentation pages to check request schemas, model limits, and new features:

- `gemini_search_docs`: Searches Gemini API documentation by topic or query.
- `gemini_get_doc`: Reads the full Markdown content of a specific documentation page.

## Gemini API plugin  {% id="gemini-api-plugin" %}

If you use **Antigravity**, the **Gemini API plugin** is the fastest way to set up your workspace. It bundles the Gemini Docs MCP server, all official Gemini skills (`gemini-api-dev`, `gemini-live-api-dev`, `gemini-omni-flash-api`), and API key tools in one download.

- **Install in Antigravity (UI):** Go to **Settings > Customizations > Build with Google Plugins** and download **Gemini API**.
- **Install with the CLI:**  ```bash
  agy plugin install https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-skills
  ```

| Method | How to use | Why use it |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Accept header (content negotiation)** | Send `Accept: text/markdown` on any `/docs/...` URL | Gets raw Markdown from the same URL you visit in a browser without changing the path. |
| **Direct `.md` URLs** | Add `.md` to any doc URL (such as `/docs/coding-agents.md`) | Gives you a clean Markdown link to share in prompts, `AGENTS.md` files, or scripts. |
| **`llms.txt` index** | [`https://aistudio.google.com/llms.txt`](https://aistudio.google.com/llms.txt) | Lists every documentation page with links to each raw Markdown file. |

| **`llms-full.txt` file** | [`https://aistudio.google.com/llms-full.txt`](https://aistudio.google.com/llms-full.txt) | Combines all Gemini API documentation pages into a single file for full context loading. |
| **Discovery headers** | Included on all `/docs` HTTP responses | Sets `Link` and `X-Llms-Txt` headers, and adds an `AI Agent Context` block to Markdown pages to point agents to the documentation indexes. |

To fetch Markdown from any documentation URL using the `Accept` header:

```bash
curl --header "Accept: text/markdown" https://aistudio.google.com/docs/interactions-overview
```

You can also click **Copy page** at the top of any documentation page to copy the Markdown source to your clipboard.

## Recommended project rules (`AGENTS.md`)  {% id="project-rules" %}

A project rules file (`AGENTS.md`, `.cursorrules`, or `CLAUDE.md`) sets baseline rules that load at the start of every agent session. Add these guidelines to your project root so coding agents default to current models and SDKs:

```markdown
# Gemini API Guidelines

- Before writing Gemini API code, consult the `geminiDocs` MCP server (`gemini_search_docs` / `gemini_get_doc`) or `https://aistudio.google.com/llms.txt`.
- Always use the current Google Gen AI SDK (`google-genai` for Python, `@google/genai` for TypeScript/JavaScript). Never use legacy SDKs (`google-generativeai` or `@google/generative-ai`).
- Use the Interactions API (`client.interactions.create`) for new applications unless a specific feature requires `generateContent`.
- Use current recommended models (see https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models) and avoid deprecated models.
```

## Verify and troubleshoot  {% id="verification-troubleshooting" %}

### Verify your setup  {% id="verify-setup" %}

To test your setup, ask your coding agent:

```none
Look up the request schema for the Gemini Interactions API in the documentation.
```

A configured agent will use `gemini_search_docs` on the `geminiDocs` MCP server and write code using `client.interactions.create` with the `google-genai` or `@google/genai` SDK.

### Status commands  {% id="status-commands" %}

| Environment | MCP verification | Skills verification |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Claude Code** | Run `/mcp` | Run `/skills` |
| **Cursor** | Open **Settings > Features > MCP** | Open **Settings > Rules** |
| **OpenAI Codex** | Run `codex mcp list` | Check `.codex/skills/` or `~/.codex/skills/` |
| **Antigravity** | Open **Customizations > Connections** | Open **Customizations > Rules** or run `/skills list` |
| **VS Code (Copilot)** | Open **Extensions > MCP** or Output panel | Click **Select Tools** in Copilot Chat |

### Troubleshooting  {% id="troubleshooting" %}

- **Skill or MCP server not detected:** Restart your editor (Cursor or VS Code) or terminal session (Claude Code or Codex). Most agents load MCP servers and skills only when they start.
- **Global skill conflict:** If your agent ignores a globally installed skill, install the skill in your project root without `--global`:  ```bash
  npx skills add google-gemini/gemini-skills --skill gemini-api-dev
  ```

- **Rules ignored:** Make sure your `AGENTS.md`, `.cursorrules`, or `CLAUDE.md` file is in the root directory of your project.

# Getting started

This guide gets you started with the Gemini API using the [Interactions
API](/docs/interactions-overview). You'll make your first API call in under a
minute and explore text generation, multimodal understanding, image generation,
structured output, tools, function calling, agents, and background execution.

The Interactions API is available through the
[Python](https://github.com/googleapis/python-genai) and
[JavaScript](https://github.com/googleapis/js-genai) SDKs, as well as through
REST.

{% callout type="info" %}
  Building with an AI coding agent? Copy this setup prompt into your agent, or
  connect our [MCP server and skills](/docs/coding-agents) for live documentation
  updates.

```none
  Set up my Gemini API project using the Interactions API and the latest models. Read https://aistudio.google.com/docs/get-started.md first (every page under https://aistudio.google.com/docs/ is available as Markdown when you add `.md`, or via https://aistudio.google.com/llms.txt).
  1. Install `google-genai` (Python) or `@google/genai` (JS/TS) for this project.
  2. Check `GEMINI_API_KEY`, or prompt me to create one at https://aistudio.google.com/apikey.
  3. Ask if I want to add the `gemini-api-dev` skill and Docs MCP server from https://aistudio.google.com/docs/coding-agents.md.
  4. When we are set up, run one `client.interactions.create` test call, show me the reply, and ask what I want to build.
  ```

{% /callout %}

## 1. Get an API key  {% id="get-api-key" %}

To use the Gemini API, you need to have an API key to authenticate your
requests, enforce security limits, and track usage to your account.

*   Google AI Studio automatically creates a project and API key for new users.
  You can copy it from the [API keys
  page](https://aistudio.google.com/api-keys).
*   If you need a new key, click **Create API key** in AI Studio and follow the
  dialog to add a new key-project pair.
*   Additional projects and projects imported from Google Cloud may need
  [project verification](/docs/verification) before they can use the free
  tier.

{% button href="https://aistudio.google.com/apikey" variant="ais" %}Create a Gemini API Key{% /button %}

Set your key as an environment variable:

```bash
export GEMINI_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"
```

To increase your rate limits, click **Set up billing** on the [API
keys](https://aistudio.google.com/api-keys) page or see the [Billing
guide](/docs/billing).

## 2. Install the SDK and make your first call  {% id="2-install-the-sdk-and-make-your-first-call" %}

Install the SDK and generate text with a single API call.

{% tabs %}
  {% tab label="Python" %}
  Install the SDK:

```bash
  pip install -U google-genai
  ```

Initialize the client and make a request:

```python
  from google import genai

client = genai.Client()

interaction = client.interactions.create(
      model="gemini-4-hydrogen",
      input="Explain how AI works in a few words"
  )
  print(interaction.output_text)
  ```

{% /tab %}

{% tab label="REST" %}
  ```bash
  curl -X POST "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/interactions" \
    -H "x-goog-api-key: $GEMINI_API_KEY" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H "Api-Revision: 2026-05-20" \
    -d '{
      "model": "gemini-4-hydrogen",
      "input": "Explain how AI works in a few words"
    }'
  ```

**Response:**

When using REST, the API returns the full `Interaction` resource containing
    metadata, usage statistics, and the step-by-step history of the turn.

{% /tab %}

{% tab label="CLI" %}
  ```bash
  curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google-gemini/gemini-api-cli/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
  gemini-api generate "Explain how AI works in a few words"
  ```

{% /tab %}

{% /tabs %}

While the SDKs expose the full response, they also provide convenience
properties like `interaction.output_text` and `interaction.output_image` to
access final outputs directly. Learn more about the response structure in the
[Interactions overview](/docs/interactions-overview) or read the [text
generation guide](/docs/text-generation) for details on system instructions and
generation config.

{% tab label="REST" %}
  ```bash
  curl -X POST "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/interactions?alt=sse" \
    -H "x-goog-api-key: $GEMINI_API_KEY" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H "Api-Revision: 2026-05-20" \
    --no-buffer \
    -d '{
      "model": "gemini-4-hydrogen",
      "input": "Explain how AI works",
      "stream": true
    }'
  ```

When streaming, the server responds with a stream of server-sent events (SSE).
    Each event includes a type and JSON data.

**Response:**

```json
  event: interaction.created
  data: {"interaction":{"id":"v1_Chd...","status":"in_progress","model":"gemini-4-hydrogen"},"event_type":"interaction.created"}

event: step.start
  data: {"index":0,"step":{"type":"thought"},"event_type":"step.start"}

{% tab label="CLI" %}
  ```bash
  gemini-api generate "Explain how AI works"
  ```

{% /tab %}

{% /tabs %}

For a detailed look at handling streaming events and delta types, see the
[streaming interactions guide](/docs/streaming).

## 4. Multi-turn conversations  {% id="4-multi-turn-conversations" %}

The Interactions API supports multi-turn conversations with two approaches:

*   **Stateful (recommended)**: Continue a conversation on the server using
  `previous_interaction_id`. Ideal for most chat and agentic workflows where
  you want the server to manage history and optimize caching.
*   **Stateless**: Manage the conversation history on the client by passing all
  previous turns (including intermediate model thought and tool steps) in each
  request.

# Turn 2: Build full history
  HISTORY=$(jq -n \
    --argjson first_input '[{"type": "user_input", "content": "I have 2 dogs in my house."}]' \
    --argjson model_steps "$MODEL_STEPS" \
    --argjson second_input '[{"type": "user_input", "content": "How many paws are in my house?"}]' \
    '$first_input + $model_steps + $second_input')

curl -X POST "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/interactions" \
    -H "x-goog-api-key: $GEMINI_API_KEY" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H "Api-Revision: 2026-05-20" \
    -d "{
      \"model\": \"gemini-4-hydrogen\",
      \"store\": false,
      \"input\": $HISTORY
    }"
  ```

## 5. Multimodal understanding  {% id="5-multimodal-understanding" %}

Gemini models understand images, audio, video, and documents natively. Pass
media alongside text in a single request.

{% tabs %}
  {% tab label="Python" %}
  ```python
  import base64
  from google import genai

client = genai.Client()

# Load a local image
  with open("sample.jpg", "rb") as f:
      image_bytes = f.read()
  image_b64 = base64.b64encode(image_bytes).decode("utf-8")

CreateModelInteraction params =
      CreateModelInteraction.builder()
          .model(Model.of("gemini-4-hydrogen"))
          .input(
              InteractionsInput.ofContent(
                  Arrays.asList(
                      TextContent.builder()
                          .text("Compare this local image and this remote audio file.")
                          .build(),
                      ImageContent.builder()
                          .data(imageB64)
                          .mimeType(ImageContentMimeType.IMAGE_JPEG)
                          .build(),
                      AudioContent.builder()
                          .uri("https://storage.googleapis.com/generativeai-downloads/data/sample.mp3")
                          .mimeType(AudioContentMimeType.AUDIO_MP3)

## 7. Use structured output  {% id="7-use-structured-output" %}

Configure the model to return JSON that matches a schema you define. Structured
output works with [Pydantic](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/) (Python) and
[Zod](https://zod.dev/) (JavaScript).

{% tabs %}
  {% tab label="Python" %}
  ```python
  from google import genai
  from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
  from typing import List, Optional

class Recipe(BaseModel):
      recipe_name: str = Field(description="Name of the recipe.")
      ingredients: List[str] = Field(description="List of ingredients.")
      prep_time_minutes: Optional[int] = Field(description="Prep time in minutes.")

client = genai.Client()

The output text block contains a valid JSON string conforming exactly to the
requested schema. To learn how to define more complex structures and recursive
schemas, see the [structured output guide](/docs/structured-output).

## 8. Use tools  {% id="8-use-tools" %}

Ground the model's response in real-time information with Google Search. The API
automatically searches, processes results, and returns citations.

  ```python
  from google import genai

client = genai.Client()

interaction = client.interactions.create(
      model="gemini-4-hydrogen",
      input="Who won the euro 2024?",
      tools=[{"type": "google_search"}]
  )

print(interaction.output_text)

    -H "Api-Revision: 2026-05-20" \
    -d '{
      "model": "gemini-4-hydrogen",
      "input": "Who won the euro 2024?",
      "tools": [{"type": "google_search"}]
    }'
  ```

## 10. Run a managed agent  {% id="10-run-a-managed-agent" %}

Managed agents run in a remote sandbox with access to tools like code execution
and file management. Pass an `agent` instead of a `model` and set
`environment="remote"`.

{% tabs %}
  {% tab label="Python" %}
  ```python
  from google import genai

client = genai.Client(http_options={"api_version": "v1beta"})

interaction = client.interactions.create(
      agent="antigravity-preview-09-2026",
      input="Write a Python script that generates the first 20 Fibonacci numbers and saves them to fibonacci.txt. Then read the file and print its contents.",
      environment="remote",
  )
  print(f"Environment: {interaction.environment_id}")
  print(interaction.output_text)
  ```

{% /tab %}

{% tab label="REST" %}
  ```bash
  curl -X POST "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/interactions" \
    -H "x-goog-api-key: $GEMINI_API_KEY" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H "Api-Revision: 2026-05-20" \
    -d '{
      "agent": "antigravity-preview-09-2026",
      "input": "Write a Python script that generates the first 20 Fibonacci numbers and saves them to fibonacci.txt. Then read the file and print its contents.",
      "environment": "remote"
    }'
  ```

{% /tab %}

{% tab label="CLI" %}
  ```bash
  gemini-api agent run "Write a Python script that generates the first 20 Fibonacci numbers and saves them to fibonacci.txt. Then read the file and print its contents." \
    --agent antigravity-preview-09-2026 \
    --body '{"environment": "remote"}'
  ```

## 11. Run tasks in the background  {% id="11-run-tasks-in-the-background" %}

Set `background=True` to run long tasks asynchronously. Poll for results with
`interactions.get()`.

{% tabs %}
  {% tab label="Python" %}
  ```python
  import time
  from google import genai

client = genai.Client()

interaction = client.interactions.create(
      model="gemini-4-hydrogen",
      input="Write a detailed analysis of the impact of artificial intelligence on modern healthcare.",
      background=True,
  )
  print(f"Started background task: {interaction.id}")
  print(f"Status: {interaction.status}")

{% /tab %}

{% tab label="REST" %}
  ```bash
  # Start a background task
  RESPONSE=$(curl -s -X POST "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/interactions" \
    -H "x-goog-api-key: $GEMINI_API_KEY" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H "Api-Revision: 2026-05-20" \
    -d '{
      "model": "gemini-4-hydrogen",
      "input": "Write a detailed analysis of the impact of artificial intelligence on modern healthcare.",
      "background": true
    }')

INTERACTION_ID=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | jq -r '.id')
  echo "Started background task: $INTERACTION_ID"

# Poll for completion
  while true; do
    RESULT=$(curl -s "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/interactions/$INTERACTION_ID" \
      -H "x-goog-api-key: $GEMINI_API_KEY" \
      -H "Api-Revision: 2026-05-20")
    STATUS=$(echo "$RESULT" | jq -r '.status')
    echo "Status: $STATUS"
    if [ "$STATUS" = "completed" ]; then
      echo "$RESULT" | jq -r '.steps[] | select(.type=="model_output") | .content[] | select(.type=="text") | .text'
      break
    elif [ "$STATUS" = "failed" ]; then
      echo "Failed"
      break
    fi
    sleep 5
  done
  ```

**Response:**

The initial response returns immediately with status `in_progress`:

```json
  {
    "id": "v1_abc123",
    "status": "in_progress",
    "object": "interaction",
    "model": "gemini-4-hydrogen"
  }
  ```

{% tab label="CLI" %}
  ```bash
  INTERACTION_ID=$(gemini-api agent run "Write a detailed analysis of the impact of artificial intelligence on modern healthcare." \
    -m gemini-4-hydrogen --background --stream=false --jq '.id')
  echo "Started background task: $INTERACTION_ID"
  # Re-run until the status is "completed"
  gemini-api agent status "$INTERACTION_ID"
  ```

{% /tab %}

# Using Gemini API keys

To use the Gemini API, you must authenticate your requests. You can
authenticate using a standard or authorization API key.

{% button href="https://aistudio.google.com/apikey" variant="ais" %}Create or view a Gemini API Key{% /button %}

## API key types: Standard versus Authorization  {% id="api-keys" %}

API keys provide access to the Gemini API, but their security characteristics
differ. The Gemini API is transitioning from standard API keys to authorization
keys to improve security:

*   **Standard API keys**: Associate requests with a Google Cloud project for
  billing and quota purposes. Standard keys don't identify a caller, which
  limits the granularity of permissions and access control they can support.

*   **Authorization (auth) keys**: Bound directly to a Google Cloud service
  account. When you use an authorization key, your requests are processed
  under the identity of that bound service account, enabling granular access
  control. Authorization keys are restricted to the Generative Language API
  (Gemini API) by default and provide fast-acting leaked key enforcement that
  quickly stops the usage of leaked keys detected by our systems.

To ensure secure usage, Gemini API will move from standard keys to auth keys:

*   **Auth keys default**: Starting May 28, 2026, all new API keys created in
  Google AI Studio are automatically created as auth keys.

*   **Unrestricted keys rejected**: The Gemini API rejects requests
  from **unrestricted standard keys**. Standard API keys that have explicit
  restrictions applied continue to work. This restriction prevents the
  unauthorized use of keys that might be shared publicly or linked to other
  services.

{% callout type="note" %}
  Requests authenticated by authorization keys are not recorded in
  Google Cloud service account usage metrics.

{% /callout %}

## Managing API keys in Google AI Studio  {% id="getting-started" %}

You can manage your projects and keys directly in [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey).

### Google Cloud projects  {% id="google-cloud-projects" %}

Every Gemini API key is associated with a [Google Cloud project](https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/creating-managing-projects).
Google Cloud projects manage billing, collaborators, and permissions. Google AI
Studio provides a lightweight interface to access these projects.

*   **Default project**: If you are a new user, Google AI Studio automatically
  creates a default Google Cloud project and API key after you accept the
  Terms of Service. You can rename this project by navigating to the
  **Projects** view in your dashboard.

*   **Existing projects**: If you already have a Google Cloud account, AI
  Studio does not create a default project. Instead, you must import your
  existing projects.

### Importing projects  {% id="import-projects" %}

By default, Google AI Studio does not display all of your Google Cloud
projects. You must import the projects you want to use:

1.   Go to [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com).

2.   Open the **Dashboard** from the left panel and select **Projects**.

3.   Click the **Import projects** button.

4.   Search for and select the Google Cloud project you want to import, then
  click **Import**.

5.   Once imported, navigate to the **API Keys** page in the dashboard to
  create a key in that project.

Imported projects may need [project verification](/docs/verification) before
they can use the Gemini API free tier. You can also
[set up billing](/docs/billing#setup-billing) to use the paid tier instead.

### Troubleshooting key creation permissions  {% id="key-permission" %}

If the **Create API key** button is unavailable and displays the message:
*"You do not have permission to create a key in this project"*, you lack the
required IAM permissions.

Ask your Google Cloud project or organization administrator to grant you a role
containing the following permissions (such as Project Editor):

*   `resourcemanager.projects.get`: Allows AI Studio to look up the project.

*   `apikeys.keys.create`: Allows key generation.

*   `serviceusage.services.enable`: Ensures the Generative Language API is
  enabled.

*   `iam.serviceAccounts.create`: Required to create the linked service account.

*   `iam.serviceAccountApiKeyBindings.create`: Binds the service account to the
  API key.

If you cannot get administrative access, you can create a new Google Cloud
project that is not associated with an organization to generate your keys.

Google AI Studio only displays keys that are unrestricted or restricted to the
Gemini API. If you can't use AI Studio, or you want to manage all of your API
keys in one place, follow the Cloud documentation on [creating an API key](https://cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/api-keys#create).
Creating a Gemini API key requires binding it to a
[service account](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-account-overview).
Projects created outside Google AI Studio may need
[project verification](/docs/verification) before they can use the free tier.

## Setting up your environment  {% id="setup-environment" %}

Once you have a key, configure your environment to use it securely in your
applications.

### Option 1: Use environment variables (Recommended)  {% id="set-api-env-var" %}

Set the environment variable `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY`. The Gemini
API client libraries automatically detect and use these variables. If both are
set, `GOOGLE_API_KEY` takes precedence.

Select your operating system to set the variable:

{% tabs %}
  {% tab label="Linux/macOS - Bash" %}
  Verify if you have a bash configuration file:

```posix-terminal
  ~/.bashrc
  ```

If not, create one and open it:

```posix-terminal
  touch ~/.bashrc && open ~/.bashrc
  ```

Add the export command at the end of the file:

```posix-terminal
  export GEMINI_API_KEY=[YOUR_API_KEY_HERE]
  ```

Save the file, then apply the changes:

```posix-terminal
  source ~/.bashrc
  ```

{% /tab %}

{% tab label="macOS - Zsh" %}
  Verify if you have a zsh configuration file:

```posix-terminal
  ~/.zshrc
  ```

If not, create one and open it:

```posix-terminal
  touch ~/.zshrc && open ~/.zshrc
  ```

Add the export command:

```posix-terminal
  export GEMINI_API_KEY=[YOUR_API_KEY_HERE]
  ```

Save the file, then apply the changes:

```posix-terminal
  source ~/.zshrc
  ```

{% /tab %}

### Critical security rules  {% id="critical-security-rules" %}

*   **Keep keys confidential**: Never check API keys into source control systems
  like Git.

*   **Never expose keys client-side in production**: Do not hardcode API keys
  directly in web or mobile apps. Keys compiled in client-side code can be
  extracted by users. To secure client-side apps, run a backend proxy
  server to make the actual API calls.

### Secret management best practices  {% id="secret-management" %}

*   **Environment variables**: Read keys from environment variables rather than
  configuration files.

*   **Secret Manager**: For production, store your keys in a secure secret store
  such as [Google Cloud Secret Manager](https://cloud.google.com/secret-manager).

*   **Billing alerts**: Set up billing alerts in the Google Cloud console to
  notify you if usage or costs spike.

### Leak response checklist  {% id="leak-response" %}

If you suspect your API key has been leaked:

1.   **Generate a new key**: Create a replacement key in Google AI Studio or the
  Cloud console.

2.   **Update your application**: Deploy your code using the new key.

3.   **Disable or delete the compromised key**: Disable the leaked key in the
  Cloud console once the new key is verified. Do not delete the old key until
  the new key is fully active to avoid application downtime.

4.   **Audit usage**: Check billing logs and API usage in the Google Cloud
  console to identify unauthorized activity.

## Restricting and securing your keys  {% id="restricting-keys" %}

Adding restrictions to your API keys minimizes the potential damage if a key is
compromised.

### Apply request origin restrictions  {% id="request-origin-restrictions" %}

Origin restrictions limit which IP addresses, websites, or applications can use
your key.

1.   Go to the [Google Cloud console credentials page](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials).

2.   Select your project, and click the name of the API key you want to restrict.

3.   Under **Application restrictions**, select **IP addresses** (or the
  appropriate restriction type for your environment).

4.   Specify the allowed IP addresses or ranges, then click **Save**.

### Securing unrestricted standard API keys  {% id="secure-unrestricted-keys" %}

To continue using the Gemini API, you must secure any unrestricted keys.

#### Method A: Restrict the key to the Gemini API only (AI Studio)  {% id="method-a-restrict-the-key-to-the-gemini-api-only-ai-studio" %}

If you only use the key for the Gemini API, secure it directly in AI Studio:

1.   On the **API Keys** page in [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/api-keys), locate keys marked with the
  **Unrestricted** label.

2.   Hover over the label and click **Add restrictions** in the dialog.

3.   Select **Restrict to Gemini API only**.

4.   Click **Restrict key** to confirm.

{% callout type="note" %}
  To restrict an API key, you must have the `apikeys.keys.update` permission
  on the associated Google Cloud project. This permission is included in roles
  like **API Keys Admin** or **Editor**.

{% /callout %}

#### Method B: Restrict the key for other services (Google Cloud console)  {% id="method-b-restrict-the-key-for-other-services-google-cloud-console" %}

If the key is shared with other Google APIs (not recommended), restrict it in
the Cloud console. **Note: Gemini API requests using this key will fail after
these restrictions are applied.**

1.   Visit the [Google Cloud console credentials page](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials).

2.   Select the project and the API key.

3.   Under **API restrictions**, select **Restrict key**.

4.   From the drop-down, select the APIs you want this key to access. Do not
  select the **Generative Language API**.

5.   Click **Save**. Create a separate, restricted key in AI Studio to continue
  using the Gemini API.

### Blocked dormant keys  {% id="blocked-keys" %}

Starting May 7, 2026, the Gemini API blocks unrestricted API keys that have
been dormant for an extended period. These keys show a **Blocked** tag in AI
Studio. You must generate a new key or use an existing restricted key to
continue.

## Migrate to an auth key  {% id="migrate-to-auth-key" %}

Follow these steps to create a new auth API key and update your applications:

1.   Go to the [AI Studio API Keys page](https://aistudio.google.com/api-keys).

2.   Check the **Key Type** column to identify any keys listed as **Standard**.

3.   Click **Create API key** to generate a new key. All new keys created in
  AI Studio are automatically created as auth keys.

4.   Copy the new auth API key.

5.   Update your application code, environment variables, and any deployment
  configurations to use the new auth API key.

6.   Test your application to confirm it works correctly with the new key.

7.   Once verified, delete or revoke your old traffic key to prevent misuse.

{% callout type="note" %}
  If you don't see your keys, you may need to import your Cloud projects
  into AI Studio. Refer to the [import projects](/docs/api-key#import-projects) section
  for instructions.

{% /callout %}

## Limitations  {% id="limitations" %}

Google AI Studio imposes the following project and key management limitations:

*   You can create a maximum of 10 projects at a time from the Google AI Studio
  **Projects** page.

*   The **API keys** and **Projects** pages display a maximum of 100 keys and 50
  projects.

*   Only API keys that are unrestricted or restricted specifically to the
  Generative Language API (Gemini API) are displayed.

For advanced project management or to modify keys with other restrictions, use
the [Google Cloud console credentials page](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials).

## Notes  {% id="notes" %}

*     **Agentic video understanding:** When using agentic video understanding,
  token usage is variable based on the content loaded by the model rather than
  full video length. This typically results in up to 88% fewer input tokens
  for long-form video, though token counts depend on query complexity and
  dynamic sampling depth (which may exceed 1 FPS for detailed visual
  segments). See [Agentic video
  understanding](/docs/video-understanding#agentic-video-understanding).

*     **Document token billing:** Tokens for the `DOCUMENT` modality (for example,
  PDFs) are billed at the image token rate. In API responses, these tokens
  appear under the `DOCUMENT` modality within `promptTokensDetails`.

*     Google AI Studio usage is free of charge in all [available
  regions](/docs/available-regions). See [Billing FAQs](/docs/billing) for
  details.

*     Prices may differ from the prices listed here and the prices offered on
  Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. For Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
  prices, see the [Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform pricing
  page](https://cloud.google.com/products/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform).

*     If you are using [dynamic retrieval](/docs/google-search) to optimize costs,
  only requests that contain at least one grounding support URL from the web
  in their response are charged for Grounding with Google Search. Costs for
  Gemini always apply. Rate limits are subject to change.

*     **Search Grounding rate limits:** On the Gemini Developer API, Grounding
  with Google Search on Gemini 3 and newer models is subject to a default
  daily rate limit of 1,500 requests per day (RPD) per project across all paid
  tiers, resetting daily at midnight Pacific Time. For high-volume production
  workloads requiring higher daily limits, consider using
  [Vertex AI](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/grounding/grounding-with-google-search#considerations),
  which provides a default quota of 1,000,000 search queries per day.

# Gemini API CLI

The Gemini API CLI (`gemini-api`) is a stateless, zero-dependency command-line client built for AI agents with shell access, scripts, and CI pipelines. Your coding agent can use it to generate text and media, analyze files, and delegate tasks to [Gemini managed agents](/docs/agents). It works with Antigravity, Claude Code, Cursor, and any standard shell environment.

Every feature runs as a standard shell command on the [Interactions API](/docs/interactions-overview). Run the same commands from an agent subprocess, your terminal, or a CI pipeline:

```bash
# 1. Install on macOS or Linux
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google-gemini/gemini-api-cli/main/scripts/install.sh | bash

# 2. Set your API key
export GEMINI_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"

# 3. Generate media, analyze a file, or launch a background managed agent
gemini-api image "Minimalist isometric icon of a cloud database" --out ./assets/db-icon.jpg
gemini-api analyze -i ./docs/quarterly-report.pdf "Summarize the key findings in three bullets."
gemini-api agent run "Compare WebRTC SFU architectures and cite sources" \
  --agent deep-research-preview-04-2026 \
  --background \
  --stream=false
```

{% callout type="note" %}
  `gemini-api` is an open-source beta release that evolves alongside the [Interactions API](/docs/interactions-overview). Breaking changes can occur between minor versions. Pin a specific [release version](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-api-cli/releases) in automated agent environments and CI pipelines.

{% /callout %}

## Choose the right Gemini tool  {% id="choose-tool" %}

Use `gemini-api` when an agent or script needs to **call** Gemini directly from the shell without adding SDK code to your project. Use the SDKs and [coding agent setup](/docs/coding-agents) when you are **building** Gemini into an application:

| Tool | What it does | When to use it |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Gemini API CLI** (`gemini-api`) | Calls Gemini models and managed agents from any shell. | Your coding agent, shell script, or CI job needs to generate media, analyze files, or run a background research agent with zero project dependencies. |
| **[Google GenAI SDKs](/docs/libraries)** | Imports Gemini client libraries into Python, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Java, or C# code. | You are building Gemini features into your application, backend service, or real-time [Live API](/docs/live-api) session. |
| **[Gemini Docs MCP & skills](/docs/coding-agents)** | Gives coding agents live documentation search and current SDK rules. | Your coding agent is writing application code that imports a Google GenAI SDK. |

- **Offline schema lookup:** Pass `--usage` to print the command tree (in [KDL](https://kdl.dev)), or `--schema` to print the JSON Schema for `--body` requests.
- **Files on disk, paths on `stdout`:** Media and transcription commands write files to disk and print only the output path, keeping binary data out of context.
- **Dry runs and structured output:** `--dry-run` validates inputs, redacts credentials, and previews the HTTP request offline. Pass `-o json`, `-o toon`, or `--jq` for machine-readable output. Add `--agent-mode` to return structured JSON errors on `stderr`, and check [exit codes](/docs/cli#exit-codes) to handle failures. Commands never prompt unless you pass `--interactive`.

- **Stateless by default:** Commands keep no hidden local state. Chain multi-step work explicitly with `--previous-interaction-id`, an uploaded `files/<id>` URI, or a background interaction ID.

With `-o json`, media commands still write the file to disk and print metadata to `stdout`:

```json
{
  "kind": "image",
  "mime_type": "image/jpeg",
  "path": "/path/to/project/assets/db-icon.jpg",
  "response_id": "v1_...",
  "size_bytes": 2914159,
  "status": "completed"
}
```

### 2. Configure authentication and verify  {% id="authentication" %}

Create an API key in [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey) (see [API keys](/docs/api-key)). Set `GEMINI_API_KEY` in your shell and your agent's subprocess environment:

```bash
export GEMINI_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"
```

On a local workstation, you can save the key in your OS keychain (macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service, or Windows Credential Manager). Pass `--no-keyring` to store the key in `~/.config/gemini-api/config.yaml` instead:

```bash
# Save to your OS keychain (or run gemini-api configure --interactive)
gemini-api configure --api-key "YOUR_API_KEY"

# Check the active credential source, then preview a request offline
gemini-api whoami
gemini-api generate "Confirm CLI setup in one sentence." --dry-run
```

{% callout type="warning" %}
  Treat `GEMINI_API_KEY` as a secret. In CI, inject the key from your secret store instead of committing it to a repository or build file.

{% /callout %}

### 3. Give your agent instructions  {% id="agent-instructions" %}

Add this snippet to your project's `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules`, or system prompt so your coding agent knows how to use `gemini-api`:

```markdown
## Gemini API CLI (`gemini-api`)

You have access to `gemini-api` through the shell. Use it to generate text or media (images, speech, music, video), analyze documents and recordings, or run and manage Gemini managed agents.

1. Run `gemini-api --help` or `gemini-api --usage` to choose a command, and `gemini-api <command> --schema` before building a `--body` JSON payload.
2. Preview unfamiliar or complex calls offline with `--dry-run -o json`.
3. For a single JSON result or `--jq` filtering on `generate` or `agent run`, pass `--stream=false -o json`.
4. To chain multi-step workflows, capture the output paths that media and transcription commands print to stdout, and the `id` values returned by `generate` or `agent run`.
```

Then prompt your coding agent as usual:

```none
Build a landing page for our developer tool. Use Gemini to generate a hero
illustration and a 15-second welcome voiceover, and start a background Deep
Research agent to compare competing CLI onboarding flows. Wire the assets and
findings into the page.
```

## Commands  {% id="commands" %}

Run `gemini-api --help` to list all commands, or `gemini-api explore` to browse them interactively.

| Group | Command | What it does |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Create | `image` | Generates or edits images (`-i`), writes a JPEG file, and prints its path. |
| Create | `tts` | Synthesizes 24 kHz mono WAV speech (one or two speakers) and prints the output path. |
| Create | `music` | Generates music tracks or loops, writes the audio file, and prints its path. |
| Create | `video` | Generates or edits MP4 clips and waits until done (`--async` returns an ID immediately). |
| Create | `generate` | Generates text and streams it to `stdout` (`--stream=false` returns one complete result). |
| Understand | `analyze` | Answers questions about PDFs, images, audio, video, CSV and text files, or public YouTube URLs. |

| Understand | `transcribe` | Writes speaker-labeled, timestamped transcripts (`md`, `text`, `json`, or `srt`) and prints the output paths. |
| Manage agents | `agent` | Runs managed agents (`run`, `status`, `cancel`, `delete-interaction`) and manages custom agent definitions (`create`, `list`, `get`, `delete`). |
| Manage agents | `environments`, `credentials`, `webhooks`, `triggers` | Configures sandbox environments, stored credentials, webhook delivery, and scheduled runs for managed agents. |
| Setup and files | `configure`, `auth`, `whoami` | Configures credentials and defaults, and shows the active auth state. |
| Setup and files | `files` | Uploads, lists, inspects, and deletes files in the Files API. |
| Setup and files | `models` | Lists available models. |

## Workflows  {% id="workflows" %}

Each command defaults to a model suited for its task. Pass `--model` (`-m`) to pick a different model. Run `gemini-api models` to list available options.

### Image generation and editing  {% id="image" %}

Agents building web or mobile UIs can generate placeholders, icons, and hero images with [Nano Banana](/docs/image-generation). Pass a generated path back in with `-i` to edit the image:

```bash
# Generate a 16:9 image at 2K resolution (512, 1K, 2K, or 4K) and capture its path
HERO_PATH=$(gemini-api image "Friendly robot mascot in a sunlit workshop, space on left for headline" \
  --aspect-ratio 16:9 \
  --image-size 2K \
  --out ./public/images/hero.jpg)

# Edit the generated image
gemini-api image "Add a winter scarf and soft snowfall outside the window" \
  -i "$HERO_PATH" \
  --out ./public/images/hero-winter.jpg
```

Pass `-i` multiple times to combine reference images, such as a character and a style guide.

### Speech synthesis  {% id="tts" %}

`gemini-api tts` synthesizes 24 kHz WAV audio for UI cues, accessibility previews, and narrated walkthroughs. The default voice is `Kore`; choose another with `--voice`. For two-speaker dialogue, label each turn in the prompt and map speakers to voices:

```bash
gemini-api tts "Build succeeded. All integration tests passed." \
  --voice Aoede \
  --out ./public/audio/build-ok.wav

gemini-api tts "Alice: Welcome to the release walkthrough! Bob: Let's look at what shipped today." \
  --multi-speaker "Alice=Kore,Bob=Puck" \
  --out ./public/audio/release-intro.wav
```

### Music and video  {% id="music-video" %}

Compose original tracks with [Lyria](/docs/music-generation), and generate MP4 clips with [Gemini Omni](/docs/video):

```bash
gemini-api music "Warm ambient synth and acoustic guitar background loop, 95 BPM" \
  --out ./public/audio/bg-loop.mp3

gemini-api video "A drone shot of a mountain landscape at sunrise." \
  --aspect-ratio 16:9 \
  --resolution 1080p \
  --out ./public/video/mountain-sunrise.mp4
```

By default, the `video` command waits for generation to finish and writes the MP4 file to disk. Pass `--async` to return an interaction ID immediately, then run `gemini-api video --resume <id> --out <path>` later. Pass `-i` to animate an existing image.

### Text generation  {% id="generate" %}

`gemini-api generate` streams text to `stdout`:

```bash
gemini-api generate "Write a one-paragraph welcome message for new users of a note-taking app."
```

Add `--stdin` to pipe text into the prompt. Pass `--previous-interaction-id` to continue an earlier interaction.

### Document analysis and transcription  {% id="analyze" %}

`analyze` answers questions about PDFs, spreadsheets, screenshots, audio and video files, and public YouTube URLs. `transcribe` writes a formatted transcript (`md`, `text`, `json`, or `srt`) to disk:

```bash
gemini-api analyze -i ./docs/product-brief.pdf "List the open questions and who owns each one." > open-questions.md

gemini-api transcribe -i ./fixtures/customer-call.mp4 --format srt --out ./fixtures/customer-call.srt
```

Pass `-i` multiple times to `analyze` to compare files, such as before-and-after screenshots.

`gemini-api` sends local files inline up to 14 MB (20 MB after base64 encoding). For larger files, upload once with `files upload --wait` and reuse the returned `files/<id>` URI:

```bash
FILE_URI=$(gemini-api files upload ./recordings/all-hands.mp4 --wait)

gemini-api analyze -i "$FILE_URI" "List action items with owners and timestamps."
gemini-api transcribe -i "$FILE_URI" --format json --out ./recordings/all-hands.json
```

### Run and manage agents  {% id="managed-agents" %}

Your coding agent can delegate multi-step research or sandboxed tasks to [Gemini managed agents](/docs/agents), such as the [Deep Research agent](/docs/deep-research). Pass `--background --stream=false` to get an interaction ID immediately instead of holding a stream open:

```bash
# Launch a Deep Research job in the background and capture its interaction ID
RESEARCH_ID=$(gemini-api agent run "Compare open-source vector index benchmarks and cite primary papers." \
  --agent deep-research-preview-04-2026 \
  --background \
  --stream=false \
  --jq '.id')

# Check status or fetch the finished result while continuing other work
gemini-api agent status "$RESEARCH_ID" -o json
```

Run `gemini-api agent cancel <id>` to stop a running job. You can also launch the [Antigravity agent](/docs/antigravity-agent) in a remote sandbox with `agent run`, or manage [custom agents](/docs/custom-agents) with `agent create`, `list`, `get`, and `delete`. See [Environments](/docs/agent-environment) to configure agent sandboxes.

## Custom request bodies  {% id="custom-bodies" %}

For options without dedicated flags, pass a raw [Interactions API](/docs/interactions-overview) JSON payload with `--body` (inline or as `@file.json`). Pass `--body` to set `response_format` schemas, function-calling tools, `generation_config`, or `"store": false`. Run `gemini-api <command> --schema` first to check valid fields:

```bash
# Inspect the JSON Schema for the request body
gemini-api generate --schema > generate-schema.json

## Exit codes  {% id="exit-codes" %}

Every command returns a typed exit code so scripts and agents can handle failures without parsing error text. For example, `3` signals an authentication problem and `2` signals invalid command syntax:

| Code | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `0` | The command succeeded. |
| `1` | Runtime or API error, such as a network failure, rate limit, or failed background job. |
| `2` | Usage or validation error, such as an unknown flag, missing input, or duplicate `--body` key. |
| `3` | Authentication or authorization failure, such as a missing or invalid API key or token. |

Run `gemini-api --help-global` to list global flags shared by every command (authentication, output, network, and diagnostics).

## Limitations  {% id="limitations" %}

- Streaming commands (`generate` and `agent run`) require `--stream=false` when combined with `-o json` or `--jq` to return a single JSON response object.
- Inline `-i` file inputs cap at 14 MB of raw file data (20 MB request payload including base64 encoding). Upload large files with `gemini-api files upload`. The Files API deletes uploaded files after 48 hours.
- `gemini-api` supports standard HTTP requests, SSE streaming, and async polling, not bidirectional WebSockets. For real-time voice and video streaming, use the [Live API](/docs/live-api) with the [Google GenAI SDKs](/docs/libraries).

## What's new in Gemini 4 Carbon  {% id="whats-new-gemini-4-carbon" %}

* **Extended verification and agentic coding:** Runs deeper build-and-verify loops across complex repositories, frontend UI design, and 3D scenes, isolating root causes and checking fixes against tests.
* **Higher precision on multimodal knowledge work:** Stronger source grounding with fewer unsupported claims across dense PDFs, spreadsheets, slides, and workspace data, paired with strict adherence to output schemas.
* **Scientific and cybersecurity reasoning:** Improved performance on formal proofs, experimental data analysis, vulnerability discovery, and root-cause patching.

metadata.title: Latest Gemini models — Gemini 4 Carbon - what's new

text:
* **Unified 1M context window and long decode:** Input, thinking, and output tokens share one 1,048,576-token window, and a single response can now go past 64K tokens, up to 1M tokens minus your input. See [Long decode](/docs/long-decode).
* **Supported in Managed Agents:** The [Antigravity agent](/docs/antigravity-agent) in Gemini Managed Agents now supports `gemini-4-carbon`.

## Choosing between Carbon, Argon, and other models  {% id="choosing-between-models" %}

Gemini 4 Carbon and [Gemini 4 Argon](/docs/whats-new-gemini-4-argon) share the same 1M unified context window, built-in tools, and per-token pricing. The main difference is how many thinking tokens each model spends per turn:

metadata.title: Latest Gemini models — Gemini 4 Carbon - what's new

text:
* **Gemini 4 Carbon (`gemini-4-carbon`):** Built for tasks that push the limits of reasoning depth. Carbon spends more thinking tokens per turn to explore thoroughly and verify its work, which increases per-turn token use and latency compared to Argon. Use it for complex root-cause debugging, architectural design, dense multimodal synthesis, scientific proofs, and security auditing.
* **Gemini 4 Argon (`gemini-4-argon`):** Our efficient Gemini 4 frontier reasoning model, ideal for most advanced software engineering and knowledge work tasks. It delivers Gemini 4 intelligence with faster responses and lower token spend per turn compared to Carbon on interactive coding, day-to-day feature work, and fast production loops.

| `low` | Fewest tokens, lowest latency | Simpler tasks and cost-sensitive work. Also works for analysis and writing tasks that need light thinking. Quality can drop on hard tasks. |
| `medium` (default) | Balanced | Recommended for most tasks, including complex code and agentic use cases. |
| `high` | Most tokens, slowest first token | Complex reasoning, hard math and science, and the most difficult code or agent tasks. Pairs well with long decode for long outputs. |

text: Background execution is the recommended way to run long decode. It runs the continuation loop server-side until the model finishes or reaches `max_output_tokens`. If you need finer-grained control over retries, backoff, and error handling (or don't want your interactions stored), you can use client-side continuation in the [Interactions API](/docs/long-decode#client-side-continuation) or the [GenerateContent API](/docs/long-decode?generate-content=true). ### Setting output token limits  {% id="setting-output-token-limits" %}

`max_output_tokens` sets the maximum combined thinking and output tokens for a response. Set it high enough that thinking doesn't cut the answer short, and low enough to limit spend when a hard prompt uses all of it.

Use these values as a starting point:

* **Standard tasks:** Keep the default of 65,536 or don't set any value.
* **Existing apps with a limit lower than 32K:** Raise `max_output_tokens` to at least 32,768. Gemini 4 Carbon can spend more of the limit on thinking than earlier models. To use fewer tokens, lower the thinking level instead.
* **Complex reasoning and coding:** Set `background: true` and set `max_output_tokens` to 131,072 or 262,144, up to 1,048,576 minus your input tokens.

### Migrate from Gemini 4 Argon  {% id="migrate-from-gemini-4-argon" %}

If you already run `gemini-4-argon`, upgrading to `gemini-4-carbon` requires no request schema changes:

* **Update model ID:** Change your model string from `gemini-4-argon` to `gemini-4-carbon`.
* **Account for longer thinking:** Carbon spends more thinking tokens per turn than Argon on complex tasks. Keep `thinking_level` at `medium` (default) unless a workload needs `high`, and make sure your `max_output_tokens` and HTTP timeouts allow for longer reasoning passes.
* **Keep Argon where speed matters:** Retain [`gemini-4-argon`](/docs/whats-new-gemini-4-argon) when you want faster responses and lower token spend per turn compared to Carbon on interactive coding, day-to-day feature work, and fast production loops.

text: ### Migrate from Gemini 3 and earlier  {% id="migrate-to-gemini-4-carbon" %}

metadata.title: Latest Gemini models — Gemini 4 Carbon - what's new

text:
* **Update model ID:** Change your target model string to `gemini-4-carbon`.
* **Review `max_output_tokens`:** If you set it explicitly today, consider raising it. We recommend at least 32,768, since Gemini 4 Carbon can spend more of the limit on thinking.
* **Configure thinking level:** Choose `low`, `medium` (default), or `high`, and test your workload at all three.
* **Move off explicit context caching:** Explicit caching (`cachedContents` / `caches.create`) is not supported on Gemini 4 Carbon. Remove calls that create or reference `cached_content` from your requests. [Implicit caching](/docs/caching) is enabled by default for prompts of at least 4,096 tokens and discounts cached input tokens by 95% on cache hits.

metadata.title: Latest Gemini models — Gemini 4 Carbon - what's new

text:
* **Remove sampling parameters:** Remove `temperature`, `top_p`, and `top_k` from your requests. If provided, they are ignored.
* **Use background execution for long outputs:** For tasks that need more than 64K tokens, set `background` to true and `max_output_tokens` greater than 65,536.
* **Increase client timeouts:** Hard prompts can take several minutes. Use background execution, or set HTTP client timeouts to at least 15 minutes.
* **Keep conversation state on the server:** Use `previous_interaction_id` for multi-turn and function calling conversations.
* **Review your cost estimates:** Every token the model processes is billed, including internal tool system instructions and function declarations when using grounding (see [Pricing](/docs/whats-new-gemini-4-carbon#pricing)).

## Pricing  {% id="pricing" %}

Gemini 4 Carbon is available at introductory pricing through November 30, 2026:

* **Input tokens:** $2.00 per 1M tokens ($4.00 starting December 1, 2026)  *   **Cached input tokens:** Implicit caching discounts cached input by 95%, to $0.10 per 1M tokens ($0.20 starting December 1, 2026).

* **Output tokens, including thinking tokens:** $10.00 per 1M tokens ($20.00 starting December 1, 2026)

Every token the model processes is counted and billed, including thinking tokens and internal tool system instructions and function declarations when using grounding. Grounding with Google Search also remains billed per query.

Gemini 4 Carbon is not available on the Free tier. For complete pricing tiers, see the [pricing page](/docs/pricing#gemini-4-carbon).

### Setting output token limits  {% id="setting-output-token-limits" %}

`max_output_tokens` sets the maximum combined thinking and output tokens for a response. Set it high enough that thinking doesn't cut the answer short, and low enough to limit spend when a hard prompt uses all of it.

Use these values as a starting point:

* **Standard tasks:** Keep the default of 65,536 or don't set any value.
* **Existing apps with a limit lower than 32K:** Raise `max_output_tokens` to at least 32,768. Gemini 4 Argon can spend more of the limit on thinking than earlier models. To use fewer tokens, lower the thinking level instead.
* **Complex reasoning and coding:** Set `background: true` and set `max_output_tokens` to 131,072 or 262,144, up to 1,048,576 minus your input tokens.

### Migrate to gemini-4-argon  {% id="migrate-to-gemini-4-argon" %}

* **Update model ID:** Change your target model string to `gemini-4-argon`.
* **Review `max_output_tokens`:** If you set it explicitly today, consider raising it. We recommend at least 32,768, since Gemini 4 Argon can spend more of the limit on thinking.
* **Configure thinking level:** Choose `low`, `medium` (default), or `high`, and test your workload at all three.
* **Move off explicit context caching:** Explicit caching (`cachedContents` / `caches.create`) is not supported on Gemini 4 Argon. Remove calls that create or reference `cached_content` from your requests. [Implicit caching](/docs/caching) is enabled by default for prompts of at least 4,096 tokens and discounts cached input tokens by 95% on cache hits.

metadata.title: Latest Gemini models — Gemini 4 Argon - what's new

text:
* **Remove sampling parameters:** Remove `temperature`, `top_p`, and `top_k` from your requests. If provided, they are ignored.
* **Use background execution for long outputs:** For tasks that need more than 64K tokens, set `background` to true and `max_output_tokens` greater than 65,536.
* **Increase client timeouts:** Hard prompts can take several minutes. Use background execution, or set HTTP client timeouts to at least 15 minutes.
* **Keep conversation state on the server:** Use `previous_interaction_id` for multi-turn and function calling conversations.
* **Review your cost estimates:** Every token the model processes is billed, including internal tool system instructions and function declarations when using grounding (see [Pricing](/docs/whats-new-gemini-4-argon#pricing)).

## Understanding reasoning levels  {% id="understanding-reasoning-levels" %}

Gemini 3.8 Flash gives you flexible control over latency and intelligence by adjusting the model's thinking level:

* **Low thinking effort**: Reduces time-to-answer for latency-critical tasks like incident response pipelines, real-time chat, writing drafts, and fast data analysis.
* **Medium (default):** Best quality for most tasks. Recommended for complex code and agentic use cases, providing higher first-pass accuracy.
* **High thinking effort**: Maximizes the model's reasoning and tool orchestration capabilities. Best for deep reasoning, mathematics, and difficult multi-step tasks.

Note: `minimal` thinking level is not supported for Gemini 3.8 Flash and will return an error.

     "top_k": 40,
}

```

## Understanding reasoning levels  {% id="understanding-reasoning-levels" %}

Gemini 3.7 Flash gives developers flexible control over latency and intelligence by adjusting the model's thinking level:

* **Low thinking effort**: Reduces time-to-answer for latency-critical tasks like incident response pipelines, real-time chat, writing drafts, and fast data analysis.
* **Medium (default):** Best quality for most tasks. Recommended for complex code and agentic use cases, with higher first-pass accuracy.
* **High thinking effort**: Maximizes the model's ability to think and use tools. Best for complex reasoning, hard math, and difficult coding and agent tasks. Allows extended thoughts and function calls, with higher token consumption and cost.

To configure thinking levels in Gemini 3.7 Flash:

metadata.title: Latest Gemini models — Gemini 3.7 Flash - what's new

text:
```python
from google import genai

client = genai.Client()

interaction = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-3.7-flash",
    input="Analyze this payment processing pipeline for race conditions during retry attempts and rewrite the transaction locks safely.",
    generation_config={
        "thinking_level": "medium"  # Balanced reasoning effort for complex tasks
    }
)

print(interaction.output_text)
```

For multi-language code examples (JavaScript, Java, Go, REST) and in-depth reasoning concepts, see [Understanding reasoning levels in Gemini 3.8 Flash](/docs/whats-new-gemini-3.8#understanding-reasoning-levels).

text:
### Thought preservation  {% id="thought-preservation" %}

The model maintains intermediate reasoning across multi-turn conversations
automatically. When present in the conversation history, reasoning context
carries forward, which improves performance on complex multi-step tasks like
iterative debugging and code refactoring. No API changes needed:

metadata.title: Latest Gemini models — Gemini 3.5 Flash - what's new

text:
*   **Interactions API**: Thoughts are already preserved automatically. No change in behavior.
*   **GenerateContent API**: Beginning with Gemini 3.5 Flash, the model uses reasoning context from all previous turns when thought signatures are present in the conversation history. To enable this, pass the full, unmodified conversation history (including [thought signatures](/docs/thinking#signatures)) in `contents`. The SDKs handle this automatically.

metadata.title: Latest Gemini models — Gemini 3.5 Flash - what's new

text:
## Parameter updates and best practices in Gemini 3.x  {% id="parameter-updates" %}

The following apply to **all Gemini 3.x models**, including Gemini 3.5 Flash.

metadata.title: Latest Gemini models — Gemini 3.5 Flash - what's new

text:
*   **`temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`**: we strongly recommend not changing the default values. Gemini 3's reasoning capabilities are optimized for the default settings.
*   Use `thinking_level` instead of `thinking_budget`.
*   **Function calling response matching**: `id`, `name`, and response count must match the preceding calls.
*   **Multimodal function responses**: include multimodal content inside the function response, not outside it.
*   **Inline instructions in function responses**: append to the function response text, not as separate parts.
*   **Reduce unnecessary tool calls**: Use lower thinking levels or experiment with system instructions to reduce tool calls in agentic workflows.

See the sections below for how to update your code.

metadata.title: Latest Gemini models — Gemini 3.5 Flash - what's new

text:
### Sampling parameters (no longer recommended)  {% id="sampling-parameters" %}

`temperature`, `top_p`, and `top_k` are no longer recommended for all Gemini 3.x
models. Gemini 3's reasoning capabilities are optimized for the default
settings. **Remove these parameters from all requests.**

```python
# ⚠️ Remove these parameters (not recommended)
generation_config = {
    "temperature": 0.7,
    "top_p": 0.9,
    "top_k": 40,
}
```

To ensure determinism, we recommend defining a system instruction with explicit
rules for your specific use case.

metadata.title: Latest Gemini models — Gemini 3.5 Flash - what's new
Latest Gemini models — Gemini 3.5 Flash - what's new

text:
### Function calling: strict response matching  {% id="function-calling" %}

The Interactions API already errors on mismatched function responses. The
GenerateContent API does not yet error, but mismatched responses cause the model
to return empty responses with `finish_reason: STOP` in most cases. Always
follow these conventions:

| Requirement | Details |
| :--- | :--- |
| Include `id` | Every `FunctionResponse` must include the `id` from the corresponding `FunctionCall` |
| Match `name` | The `name` in the response must match the `name` in the call |
| Match counts | Return exactly one `FunctionResponse` for each `FunctionCall` received |

text:
### Reducing unnecessary tool calls  {% id="reducing-tool-calls" %}

If you experience an overuse of tool calls, two techniques help minimize them:

1.    **Start by reducing the thinking level** (`medium`, `low`, or `minimal`):
  Higher thinking levels encourage the model to use more tools to explore and
  verify, so lowering the level can reduce tool calls.

2.    **Add a system instruction:** If overuse persists after adjusting the
  thinking level, consider a prompt that restricts tool usage. For example:

```text
  You have a limited action budget of <n> tool calls. Use them efficiently.
  ```

text:
*   [**Thinking**](/docs/thinking)**:** Encrypted reasoning context preserved across API calls. Automatic in the Interactions API; implicit in GenerateContent.
*   [**Structured outputs with tools**](/docs/structured-output)**:** Combine JSON mode with built-in tools (Search, URL context, code execution, function calling).
*   [**Multimodal function responses**](/docs/function-calling#multimodal)**:** Return images, audio, and other media in function call results.
*   [**Code execution with images**](/docs/code-execution#images)**:** Execute code that processes and generates images.
*   [**Combined tool use**](/docs/tool-combination)**:** Use built-in tools and custom function calling in the same request.

text:
*   [**Media resolution**](/docs/media-resolution)**:** Fine-grained control over token allocation for image, video, and PDF inputs. Gemini 3 models support per-content-item resolution settings (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `ultra_high`) for mixed-fidelity prompts.
*   [**Thought signatures**](/docs/thinking#signatures)**:** Encrypted
  representations of the model's internal reasoning. Required for multi-turn
  function calling in stateless mode; managed automatically by the
  Interactions API and the official SDKs.

text:
## Prompting best practices  {% id="prompting-best-practices" %}

Gemini 3.x models are reasoning models, which changes how you should prompt.

text:
*   **Precise instructions:** Be concise. Gemini 3.x responds best to direct,
  clear instructions. Verbose or complex prompt engineering techniques
  designed for older models may cause the model to over-analyze.
*   **Output verbosity:** By default, Gemini 3 and 3.1 is less verbose and
  prefers direct, efficient answers. If your use case requires a
  conversational tone, steer the model explicitly in your prompt (for example,
  "Explain this as a friendly, talkative assistant").
*   **Context management:** When working with large datasets (such as entire
  books, codebases, or long videos), place your specific instructions or
  questions at the end of the prompt, after the data context. Anchor the
  model's reasoning by starting your question with a phrase like, "Based on

## Limitations  {% id="limitations" %}

*   Image segmentation is not supported in Gemini 3.x. For segmentation
  workloads, continue using Gemini 2.5 Flash with thinking off, or
  [Gemini Robotics-ER 1.6](/docs/robotics-overview).

## FAQ  {% id="faq" %}

metadata.title: Latest Gemini models — Gemini 3.5 Flash - what's new

text:
1.  **What is the knowledge cutoff for Gemini 3.5 Flash?** Gemini 3.5 Flash has
  a knowledge cutoff of January 2025. For more recent information, use the
  [Search Grounding](/docs/google-search) tool.
2.  **What are the context window limits?** Gemini 3.5 Flash supports a 1
  million token input context window and up to 65k output tokens.
3.  **Will my old `thinking_budget` code still work?** Yes, `thinking_budget` is
  still supported for backward compatibility, but we recommend migrating to
  `thinking_level` for more predictable performance. Don't use both in the
  same request.
4.  **Does Gemini 3.5 Flash support the Batch API?** Yes. See the
  [Batch API](/docs/batch-api) guide for details.
5.  **Is Context Caching supported?** Yes, [Context Caching](/docs/caching) is
  supported.

metadata.title: Latest Gemini models — Gemini 3.5 Flash - what's new

text:
6.  **Which tools are supported?** Gemini 3.5 Flash supports
  [Google Search](/docs/google-search),
  [Grounding with Google Maps](/docs/maps-grounding),
  [File Search](/docs/file-search), [Code Execution](/docs/code-execution),
  [URL Context](/docs/url-context), and standard
  [Function Calling](/docs/function-calling), including
  [combined tool use](/docs/tool-combination), and
  [Computer Use](/docs/computer-use).

### Stable  {% class="hide-from-toc" id="stable" %}

Points to a specific stable model. Stable models usually don't change. Most
production apps should use a specific stable model.

For example: `gemini-3.6-flash`.

### Preview  {% class="hide-from-toc" id="preview" %}

Points to a preview model which may be used for production. Preview models will
typically have billing enabled, might come with more restrictive rate limits and
will be deprecated with at least 2 weeks notice.

For example: `gemini-2.5-flash-preview-09-2025`.

### Latest  {% class="hide-from-toc" id="latest" %}

Points to the latest release for a specific model variation. This can be a
stable, preview or experimental release. This alias will get hot-swapped with
every new release of a specific model variation. A **2-week notice** will be
provided through email before the version behind latest is changed.

For example: `gemini-flash-latest`.

### Experimental  {% class="hide-from-toc" id="experimental" %}

Points to an experimental model which will typically not be suitable for
production use and come with more restrictive rate limits. We release
experimental models to gather feedback and get our latest updates into the hands
of developers quickly.

Experimental models are not stable and availability of model endpoints is
subject to change.

# Text generation

The Gemini API can generate text output from text, images, video, and audio
inputs.

Here's a basic example:

{% tabs %}
  {% tab label="Python" %}
  ```python
  from google import genai

client = genai.Client()

interaction = client.interactions.create(
      model="gemini-4-hydrogen",
      input="How does AI work?"
  )
  print(interaction.output_text)
  ```

{% /tab %}

{% tab label="JavaScript" %}
  ```javascript
  import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";

const ai = new GoogleGenAI({});

The most common helper is **`interaction.output_text`** (String), which returns
the last text blocks in the model's response. If the response is split
across multiple consecutive `TextContent` blocks, it automatically joins them.
Note that `.output_text` does not include earlier text blocks separated by
non-text content (such as thoughts, images, audio, or tool calls). For complex
or interleaved multimodal responses, you must manually iterate over `steps`
instead.

Refer to the [Interactions API reference](/api-reference/interactions-api)
for a complete list of configurable parameters and their
descriptions.

## Multimodal inputs  {% id="multimodal-input" %}

The Gemini API supports multimodal inputs, allowing you to combine text with
media files. The following example demonstrates providing an image:

{% tabs %}
  {% tab label="Python" %}
  ```python
  from google import genai

client = genai.Client()

uploaded_file = client.files.upload(file="path/to/organ.jpg")

File uploadedFile =
      client.files.upload(
          new java.io.File("path/to/organ.jpg"),
          UploadFileConfig.builder().mimeType("image/jpeg").build());

CreateModelInteraction params =
      CreateModelInteraction.builder()
          .model(Model.of("gemini-4-hydrogen"))
          .input(
              InteractionsInput.ofContent(
                  Arrays.asList(
                      TextContent.builder().text("Tell me about this instrument").build(),
                      ImageContent.builder()
                          .uri(uploadedFile.uri().orElse(""))
                          .mimeType(
                              ImageContentMimeType.of(uploadedFile.mimeType().orElse("image/jpeg")))
                          .build())))
          .build();

## Streaming responses  {% id="streaming-responses" %}

By default, the model returns a response only after the entire generation
process is complete.

For more fluid interactions, use streaming to handle response chunks
as they're generated. For a comprehensive guide covering event types,
streaming with tools, thinking, agents, and image generation, see the
dedicated [Streaming interactions](/docs/streaming)
guide.

{% tabs %}
  {% tab label="Python" %}
  ```python
  from google import genai

client = genai.Client()

CreateModelInteraction params1 =
      CreateModelInteraction.builder()
          .model(Model.of("gemini-4-hydrogen"))
          .input(InteractionsInput.of("I have 2 dogs in my house."))
          .build();

Interaction interaction1 =
      client.interactions.create(CreateInteractionRequestBody.of(params1)).interaction().get();
  System.out.println("Response 1: " + interaction1.outputText().orElse(""));

CreateModelInteraction params2 =
      CreateModelInteraction.builder()
          .model(Model.of("gemini-4-hydrogen"))
          .input(InteractionsInput.of("How many paws are in my house?"))
          .previousInteractionId(interaction1.id().orElse(""))
          .build();

{% tab label="REST" %}
  ```shell
  RESPONSE1=$(curl -s -X POST "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/interactions" \
    -H "x-goog-api-key: $GEMINI_API_KEY" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H "Api-Revision: 2026-05-20" \
    -d '{
      "model": "gemini-4-hydrogen",
      "input": "I have 2 dogs in my house."
    }')

INTERACTION_ID=$(echo "$RESPONSE1" | jq -r '.id')

curl -X POST "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/interactions" \
    -H "x-goog-api-key: $GEMINI_API_KEY" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H "Api-Revision: 2026-05-20" \

## Stateless conversations  {% id="stateless-conversations" %}

By default, the Interactions API manages conversation state server-side when you
use `previous_interaction_id`. However, you can also operate in stateless mode
by managing the conversation history yourself on the client side.

To use stateless mode:

1. Set `store=false` in your request to opt out of server-side storage.
2. Maintain the conversation history as an array of **steps** on the client side.
3. In subsequent requests, pass the accumulated steps in the `input` field, and append your new turn as a `user_input` step.

# Extract the steps from response
  MODEL_STEPS=$(echo "$RESPONSE1" | jq '.steps')

# Reconstruct the full history for Turn 2 by combining:
  # 1. First user input
  # 2. Model response steps
  # 3. Second user input
  HISTORY=$(jq -n \
    --argjson first_input '[{"type": "user_input", "content": "I have 2 dogs in my house."}]' \
    --argjson model_steps "$MODEL_STEPS" \
    --argjson second_input '[{"type": "user_input", "content": "How many paws are in my house?"}]' \
    "'"'"'$first_input + $model_steps + $second_input'"'"'")

## Capabilities  {% id="capabilities" %}

All Gemini model versions are multimodal and can be utilized in a wide range
of image processing and computer vision tasks including but not limited to
image captioning, visual question and answering, image classification,
object detection and segmentation.

Gemini can reduce the need to use specialized ML models depending on your
quality and performance requirements.

The latest model versions are specifically trained improve accuracy of
specialized tasks in addition to generic capabilities, like enhanced
[object detection](/docs/image-understanding#object-detection) and [segmentation](/docs/image-understanding#segmentation).

## Limitations and key technical information  {% id="technical-details-image" %}

### File limit  {% id="file-limit" %}

Gemini models support a maximum of 3,600 image files per request.

### Token calculation  {% id="token-calculation" %}

* 258 tokens if both dimensions <= 384 pixels.
  Larger images are tiled into 768x768 pixel tiles, each costing 258 tokens.

A rough formula for calculating the number of tiles is as follows:

* Calculate the crop unit size which is roughly: `floor(min(width, height)` / 1.5).
* Divide each dimension by the crop unit size and multiply together to get the
  number of tiles.

For example, for an image of dimensions 960x540 would have a crop unit size
of 360. Divide each dimension by 360 and the number of tile is 3 * 2 = 6.

### Media resolution  {% id="media-resolution" %}

Gemini 3 introduces granular control over multimodal vision processing with the
`media_resolution` parameter. The `media_resolution` parameter determines the
**maximum number of tokens allocated per input image or video frame.**
Higher resolutions improve the model's ability to
read fine text or identify small details, but increase token usage and latency.

## Tips and best practices  {% id="tips-best-practices" %}

* Verify that images are correctly rotated.
* Use clear, non-blurry images.
* When using a single image with text, place the text prompt *before* the image in the `input` array.
